steps.body: Remember the kilo-badge from big numbers? A kilogram works exactly the same way: **kilo means ×1000.** 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams. The same badge that turned a thousand into 'kilo' on a big number now turns a thousand grams into one kilogram.
Match the badge to its meaning.

widget.prompt: Match each metric prefix to what it means.

right.label: 100 of these make one base unit
1,000 of these make one base unit

pairErrors.feedback: 1,000 of these make one base unit describes MILLI-, not centi-. Centi- means 100 make a base unit.

widget.missFeedback: Kilo climbs the ladder ×1000; centi and milli count how many small pieces fit into one base unit.
widget.successFeedback: Kilo is ×1000 bigger; centi needs 100 to make a whole; milli needs 1,000.

predict.prompt: Does the prefix 'kilo' make a unit BIGGER or SMALLER?
predict.reveal: Kilo stamps ×1000 on whatever it touches — a kilometer is a thousand meters, a kilogram a thousand grams. The prefix is the multiplier.

explanationVariants: The kilo badge means ×1000, so 1 kilogram is 1,000 grams.
Same badge, same rule: kilo always means a thousand of the base unit.

widget.prompt: 1 kilogram = how many grams? Cross the chain — the mass never changes, only the counting unit.
widget.fallbackFeedback: The prefix kilo- means a thousand: one kilogram is 1000 grams, so the crossing multiplies.
widget.successFeedback: 1000 g. That is what kilo- means — one badge of a thousand.

steps.body: Here's the useful part: the badge works **no matter what you're measuring.** Kilo means ×1000 whether it's attached to grams (mass), meters (length), or anything else. One badge system, many quantities — that's the whole point of the metric system.
The same badge, a different quantity.
explanationVariants: Kilo still means ×1000, whether it's grams or meters — 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters.
The badge doesn't care what it's measuring.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Kilo- is the same badge whatever it sits on: one kilometer is 1000 meters.
widget.successFeedback: 1000 m — the prefix carries the same factor across every unit it joins.

steps.body: Sort by badge, not by quantity.

widget.prompt: Sort each pair by which badge connects them — even though they measure different things.

items.label: 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams
items.feedback: Mass, but still the ×1000 kilo badge.

items.label: 1 kilometer = 1,000 meters
items.feedback: Length this time, but the same ×1000 kilo badge as mass.

items.label: 1 liter = 100 centiliters
items.feedback: Volume, using the same centi badge as length.

widget.missFeedback: Ignore what's being measured — just match the badge word to its multiplier.
widget.successFeedback: Kilo means ×1000 for mass AND length; centi means 100-make-one for length AND volume.

explanationVariants: The centi badge means 100 of them make one base unit — so 1 meter is 100 centimeters.
100 centimeters line up to make exactly one meter.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Centi- means a hundredth, so a meter holds 100 centimeters and the crossing multiplies.
widget.successFeedback: 100 cm. Centi- is a hundredth of the unit, so it takes 100 of them to rebuild it.

hints: Each bag is 1 kilogram — apply the kilo badge to find grams per bag.
explanationVariants: Each 1 kg bag is 1,000 g; 5 bags is 5×1,000=5,000 g.
Applying the kilo badge first, then multiplying by the bag count.

widget.prompt: A store receives 5 bags of rice, each labeled 1 kilogram. What is the total weight in grams?

commonErrors.feedback: 5 forgets to apply the kilo badge at all. Each bag is 1,000 g, so 5 bags is 5×1,000=5,000 g.
500 applies only part of the badge. Each kilogram is 1,000 g (not 100), so 5×1,000=5,000 g.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Convert one bag to grams first (×1000), then multiply by 5.

takeaways: Kilo means ×1000 of the base unit, no matter what's being measured.
Centi means 100 of the small unit make one base unit.
The same badge system works for mass, length, and volume alike.
steps.teaser: next: putting the length badges to work — converting between mm, cm, m, and km.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Kilo always means ×1000.** It doesn't matter if it's kilograms, kilometers, or kiloliters — the badge multiplies by 1,000 every time. 1 kilogram = 1,000 grams; 1 kilometer = 1,000 meters.

explanationVariants: The badge multiplies by a thousand, whatever the unit.

options.label: 100 liters
options.feedback: 100 belongs to a centi badge. Kilo means ×1000: 1,000 liters.

options.label: 10 liters
options.feedback: Too small a jump. Kilo means ×1000: 1,000 liters.
